answer: A quartz haul through a wildlife haven needs signatures from three offices with distinct owners. Each signs the carrier key and a route outside sable breeding zones. The permit desk checks the route and debits one of five seasonal slots per owner before issuing a pass. A signature copied to another key fails. One honest carrier needs 3 endorsements. A farm seeking 1,000 passes needs 3,000 endorsements from at least 600 owners. Bribery can redirect these slots, and honest carriers may wait. The desk relies on verified ownership and shared counters.
